title: Cluster 02 Drill — Cell and Nuclear Division
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 3 · 8 questions · 96 marks · cumulative over Book 3 Cluster 1 + Book 2
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b) - that is the point of the layout.

Eight questions, not ten, and here is the count. Four learning outcomes, 2(n), 2(o), 2(s) and 2(t), carry thirteen content nodes between them: the cell cycle and its phases, DNA content against chromosome number, the terminology block, the four stages of mitosis against four named structures, cytokinesis in animals and plants, the significance of mitosis, checkpoint dysregulation, prophase I, metaphase I and independent assortment, anaphase I, meiosis II, the significance of meiosis, and the mitosis-against-meiosis comparison. Add three reach-back nodes - cell signalling from Cluster 1, and centromeres, telomeres and S-phase replication from Book 2 - and you have sixteen. Eight questions at four or more concepts each carry all sixteen with none repeated. A ninth would have had to re-ask something.

Five real figures, four questions figure-led. Chapter 3.2 is the most graph-driven chapter in Book 3 at 44.1% figure-led, and data and figure interpretation is 33.5% of Book 3 as a whole. Every figure is the real image from the paper the question came from, not a redrawing.

One MCQ only, and it is the specimen's own. Q5(a) is 9477 Specimen Paper 1 Question 17 word for word. You have to judge all four statements and all four options, not pick a letter.

Cumulative. Q7(a) needs the receptor tyrosine kinase and the phosphorylation cascade said cold from Cluster 1. Q4 runs on centromeres and telomeres as non-coding DNA from Book 2, and Q3(c) and Q8 need semi-conservative replication in S phase. A Cluster 1 or Book 2 gap surfacing here is worth more than a clean Cluster 2 answer, so say it out loud when it happens.

What the marks reward. Name the exact stage at which each event happens - an examiner report in this file calls vague-across-stages description the commonest failure. Write non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes in full. State both sides of every comparison positively, because schemes reject yes-or-no comparisons twice over. Keep the centromere dividing apart from the kinetochore microtubules shortening. Say cell division, never cell growth, whenever the word uncontrolled is in play. Quote figures off any graph you are told to refer to.
los_html:
Learning outcomes this cluster owns (9477 Core Idea 2)
2(n) the mitotic cell cycle and the main stages of mitosis, including the behaviour of chromosomes, nuclear envelope, cell surface membrane and centriolesQ1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q6
2(o) significance of the mitotic cell cycle - growth, repair, asexual reproduction - and the need to regulate it tightlyQ3, Q7, Q8
2(s) the meiotic cell cycle and the main stages of meiosis, same four structuresQ2, Q3, Q5, Q6
2(t) significance of meiosis, including how meiosis and random fertilisation lead to variationQ5, Q6, Q8
reach-back 3(m), 3(o) cell signalling, transduction and amplification (Cluster 1)Q7
reach-back 2(h) non-coding DNA: centromeres and telomeres (Book 2)Q4
reach-back 2(b) semi-conservative replication in S phase (Book 2)Q1, Q3, Q8

Scope, verified by literal search of the 9477 syllabus. LO 2(o) states that dysregulation of checkpoints causing uncontrolled cell division and cancer is required but details of the mechanism are not required, and cyclin, CDK and MPF return zero hits. Nothing here tests them. LO 2(s) expects the main stage names but not the sub-divisions of prophase, so leptotene through diakinesis are out. Apoptosis, karyotype and telomerase return zero hits and are never a valid answer here. Cytokinesis, kinetochore, bivalent, chiasma and independent assortment lose the word but keep the biology - the cell surface membrane is named in 2(n) and 2(s), and 2(t) asks how meiosis leads to variation - so the processes are tested and no mark hangs on the label alone.

Nothing from Books 4 to 9, and nothing from Book 3 chapters 3.3 or 3.4. Cancer genetics and stem cells are not studied yet, so no question needs them. Q7(c) goes exactly as far as LO 2(o) goes and stops.
